title: Belkin 8-Outlet Surge Protection Strip with 2.4 Amp USB Charging $39, 6-Outlet $29 + Delivery ($0 Prime/ $59 Spend) @ Amazon AU
body:
Deal: Belkin 8-Outlet Surge Protection Strip with 2.4 Amp USB Charging $39, 6-Outlet $29 + Delivery ($0 Prime/ $59 Spend) @ Amazon AU

[Nutrino] clicked link "You last purchased this item on 3 Dec 2025" $24. yea nah.
[Fergy1987] Mine said I purchased it in 2021 for $44…..dammit…. hands in Ozbargain card
[LowRange] Last purchased for 19.4 Bitcoins in 2010.
[Blitzfx] That was a good deal https://www.ozbargain.com.au/node/937156
[erd] Best powerboard is the one that you forgot that it was plugged in somewhere
[PainToad] Purchased 1898 for 3 chickens and a goat.
[andresampras] Big spender eh. Bet you had a moat around your castle
[Big L] "Last purchased this item for three magic beans, eBay marketplace, 1 Apr 2001"
[M00Cow] i wonder which naughty bot keeps neg'ing comments under this thread.
[bond008] Price Beat at officeworks
https://www.officeworks.com.au/shop/officeworks/p/belkin-8-o…
[piupiupiu] For those looking to PB at Officeworks, get them to beat Bunnings , less of a hassle that way. Occasionally you can get staff member who’d say no to Amazon.
[ThatDealsGuy] Actually had a better price at Good Guys. He gave it to me for $34 after i showed him Bunning had it for $39.
Used a $20 store voucher I got after buying a fridge last month so got it for $14 :)))
[Lizard Spock] I've had mine for 7 years without any issues. Only one annoying thing is that my computer monitor briefly turns off whenever I print something (all office devices running off this powerboard).
[Elyxar] My laser printer uses 900W on startup then 10W idle. I actually haven't measured how much during print. Sounds like you might be pushing the limit.
[Jimothy Wongingtons] Cheers was waiting for a decent price for another one.
[skibidigrimacmoggr67] ok i thought I got confused by the orientation of the sockets in the last deal.
but no mine is the exact one.
but I guess depends what you plug which is the problem.
I plug a smart plug which goes "up" so it blocks the opposite socket on this board.
but now I had a look and most older "power supply brick" actually goes "down" when hanging on the wall. so I guess for those it would be ideal.
but for most smart plug which goes up this direction of the sockets causes the opposite one to be commpletely blocked.
[Dogstar] Yup. The Tapo plugs are a huge problem. Never understood why they weren't just flipped design wise. Seems like they were meant for direct placement into a wall socket, but regardless i think they'd still work either way.
[bogak] Ah the Belkin powerboard with the massive 900 joules of surge protection.
[railspider] Not much available in aus for a reasonable price that offer >900 joules…
[bogak] Maybe not but I wouldn't be plugging my $3000 computer gear in this thing and expect it to protect it when a surge happens.
[YoshiKara] If you have a 3000 dollar computer just buy a damn UPS for it instead of relying on this
[GreenGuava] If anyone is wondering, the 2.4A is shared between the two USB ports
https://www.belkin.com/au/support-article/?articleNum=111707
[hollykryten] Yes it's rather slow charging. I've been using the 6 outlet version for a few years and it used to take ages to charge the smartphone.
[GoodUsername] I had the switch on one of these start to stick in the middle after a reasonable amount of use - could see and feel it wasn't clicking all the way. It wasn't causing electrical issues at least. Got a replacement under warranty at Good Guys and no troubles since with this one.
[SoTightEcoLPI] I've got the 8 pack version x 3, all round the house. Solid performance. Even with the server and nas.
